releases.notes:
## Added

- New `routingMode` setting, also at the top of the settings screen: `QUALITY` (default), `BALANCED` or `LIGHT`. `BALANCED` uses much less CPU while walking with nearly the same routes, and `LIGHT` uses the least, on a single core, at the cost of a few more small detours.
- Coordinates posted in chat (like `90 64 -120`) can be clicked to set the destination. Shift+click can be set to add a stop instead.
- Going between the Overworld and the Nether no longer clears the destination: it carries over to the other side's coordinates, and returning restores the exact original.

## Improved

- The first route to a far destination appears sooner.
- Long Nether routes take fewer detours: XaeroNav no longer mistakes a cliff on the map for an easy way up when choosing which way to go.

releases.notes:
## Added

- Routes by minecart. XaeroNav remembers the rails you have seen in each world and dimension, and when you carry a minecart or one is already sitting on the rails, routes can ride them, even to rails outside your render distance. The HUD tells you where to get on and when to get off.
- Routes on mounts. While riding a horse, donkey, mule, skeleton horse, zombie horse or camel, the route stays on paths your mount can walk and jump, keeps out of water, and tells you where to jump. If the way on needs you to get off, the HUD says where.
- While riding a happy ghast, you get the same flying guidance as with an elytra. While riding a nautilus, routes follow the water.
- A boat-shaped outline marks where to place your boat.
- Stops on the way. Right-click the map or a waypoint to add places to visit before your destination (up to 10), either slotted in where they add the least detour or added to the end. The route on the map and in the world carries on through every stop to the destination.

## Fixed

- Pointing at a forest or a huge mushroom on the map no longer makes you climb the tree: the destination is the ground at its foot.
- Long Nether routes take fewer detours around large lava seas. In places Xaero's map has not covered yet, the route can still change course as the map fills in.
- Standing on soul sand and similar blocks no longer makes the route start below the floor, which kept the route line from appearing at your feet and made it recalculate over and over.

releases.notes:
## Added

- Minecraft 1.21.3 support, on NeoForge 21.3 or newer, Forge 53.1.2 or newer, and Fabric with Fabric Loader 0.15.11 or newer and Fabric API 0.114.1 or newer.
- Minecraft 1.20.6 support, on NeoForge 20.6 or newer, Forge 50.2.1 or newer, and Fabric with Fabric Loader 0.15.11 or newer and Fabric API 0.100.8 or newer.
- Minecraft 1.20.2 support, on Forge 48 or newer and Fabric with Fabric Loader 0.15.11 or newer and Fabric API 0.91.6 or newer.
- More Minecraft versions on Fabric, using an existing jar: 26.1 and 26.1.1 (the 26.1.2 jar), 1.21.9 (1.21.10), 1.21.6 and 1.21.7 (1.21.8), 1.21 (1.21.1), 1.20.5 (1.20.6) and 1.20.3 (1.20.4). Xaero no longer updates its mods for some of these, so use the versions listed in the [installation instructions](https://github.com/Narcissus-tazetta/XaeroNav#installation). On 1.21 and 1.20.3, use World Map 1.41.2 with Minimap 25.3.2 if you want both.
- New `strictLimits` setting (off by default, also in the settings screen): keeps the limits on bridge length, time underwater, fall damage, risky jumps and blocks carried even when no route fits them, and tells you on the HUD that no way exists within them.

## Improved

- While gliding under open sky in the Overworld or the End, a pale yellow beam marks where to land, with a direction arrow and the distance on the HUD. For an underground destination, it marks where to land before you continue on foot.
- Gliding routes under a roof and in the Nether are found faster and take fewer unnecessary detours.
- Walking routes keep a block away from lava, the void and deadly drops when a way nearby allows it.
- Gliding routes are shorter by default. If you already have a config file, your current value is kept; set `flightHeuristicWeight` to `1.5` to get the new default.

## Fixed

- Routes no longer send you back and forth between the two sides of an unfinished bridge.
- The sky-blue gliding route now starts from the closest point on the route instead of from where you are.
- The HUD no longer says guidance continues when the route ends at a known dead end.
- Clearing navigation, arriving, or taking off now stops the previous route search instead of leaving it running in the background.
- On Forge versions too old for XaeroNav, the game now shows the version it needs instead of crashing at startup: Forge 49.1.10 on 1.20.4, 52.1.2 on 1.21.1, 54.1.5 on 1.21.4 and 55.0.24 on 1.21.5.

## Added

- Minecraft 26.3 support, on Forge 66.0.9 or newer and on Fabric with Fabric Loader 0.19.0 or newer and Fabric API 0.161.0 or newer.
- Minecraft 26.2 support, on NeoForge 26.2.0.88 or newer, Forge 65.1.3 or newer, and Fabric with Fabric Loader 0.19.0 or newer and Fabric API 0.161.0 or newer.
- Minecraft 26.1.2 support, on NeoForge 26.1.2.112 or newer, Forge 64.1.3 or newer, and Fabric with Fabric Loader 0.19.0 or newer and Fabric API 0.155.3 or newer.
- Minecraft 1.21.10 support, on NeoForge 21.10.64 or newer, Forge 60.1.15 or newer, and Fabric with Fabric Loader 0.17.0 or newer and Fabric API 0.138.4 or newer.
- Minecraft 1.21.8 support, on NeoForge 21.8.54 or newer, Forge 58.1.22 or newer, and Fabric with Fabric Loader 0.16.13 or newer and Fabric API 0.136.1 or newer.
- Minecraft 1.21.5 support, on NeoForge 21.5 or newer, on Forge 55 or newer, and on Fabric with Fabric Loader 0.16.10 or newer and Fabric API 0.128.2 or newer.
- Minecraft 1.21.4 support, on NeoForge 21.4 or newer, on Forge 54 or newer, and on Fabric with Fabric Loader 0.16.9 or newer and Fabric API 0.119.4 or newer.
- Minecraft 1.20.4 support, on NeoForge 20.4 or newer, on Forge 49 or newer, and on Fabric with Fabric API 0.97.3 or newer.
- Minecraft 1.19.2 support, on Forge 43 or newer and on Fabric with Fabric API 0.77.0 or newer.
- Minecraft 1.18.2 support, on Forge 40 or newer and on Fabric with Fabric API 0.77.0 or newer.
- The 1.21.1 NeoForge jar also runs on Minecraft 1.21 with NeoForge 21.0 or newer, and the 1.20.1 jars also run on Minecraft 1.20, on Forge 46 or newer and on Fabric with Fabric API 0.83.0 or newer.

## Improved

- The map of the area around you that XaeroNav builds for routing uses about 40% less memory (at most about 270 MB instead of about 460 MB) and updates faster. Routes are unchanged.
- Walking lines on flat ground are drawn as straight lines instead of grid-shaped zigzags, so following them is shorter.
- When a shorter way is found as you get close to the destination on a long trip, the route now switches to it more readily.

## Fixed

- Starting deep underground no longer sends you on a long detour at depth before climbing up; the route now uses a nearby way up when there is one.
- Underwater, the route no longer has you dig through blocks as if you were on land; digging there is much slower, so it now prefers swimming around or surfacing first.
- Heading to a far destination from a place your world map has not recorded yet (such as a cave right after teleporting) no longer leaves the route stuck, going back and forth, or being thrown away; it now heads toward the destination.
- In the End, routes to a far destination no longer stop at the edge of an island when the next island is beyond the loaded area; the route now builds the bridge toward it.
- Near some destinations that are hard to reach, the route no longer keeps flipping between two directions and sending you back and forth along the same stretch.
- Destinations deep underground close by, such as a cave below the seabed or below a mountain, are now reached instead of the route turning back and forth near them.

releases.notes:
## Improved

- The map of the area around you that XaeroNav builds for routing uses about a quarter less memory (at most about 460 MB instead of about 610 MB). Routes are unchanged.
- In the Overworld, routing uses much less memory and updates the route faster, especially near oceans and cave-filled areas.
- When you carry a boat, routes no longer tell you to take the boat across ponds and rivers where swimming is quicker once placing, breaking and picking up the boat is counted.

## Fixed

- Long routes in the End no longer turn back toward where you came from each time you reach the tip of an island, and no longer get stuck showing no route at all. Routes now bridge across to the next island toward the destination, including bridges that turn a corner, pass under a small floating island, or cross high above another island.
- In the End, a route can now start from a bridge you built yourself or from the edge of a small island.
- Placing a block a little early where the route shows a placement (for example, before stepping up to where the route climbs by placing a block under your feet) no longer sends you on a detour. The route now climbs onto the block you placed.
- In the Nether, routes no longer build a long bridge along an invisible edge of the search area when a short walk around would be quicker. Some routes were up to about 25% slower than the best route before this fix.
- Routes no longer keep a leftover V-shaped detour after heading toward a dead end and turning back.
